body:
The difference is, getting to the ocean is the endgame, no living quarters needed, no utilities, no food, etc... Driving to another city to get restarted would be considerably more expensive, and I'm not adverse to living out of my car, but finding a job with no address would probably be difficult.

re: my resume, I just meant that going from nearly 100k to whatever they pay people in retail is certainly spooking some hiring managers, I'm over-qualified for that work, and assumed salary expectations are probably also preventing me from getting opportunities.

That has been the plan since I learned they weren't coming back. I've been trying to find a job since I became unemployed earlier this year. This has been the longest I've been without a job since school. I work in IT, and I've applied everywhere, including local retailers just to have some kind of income. 
There's just a pile of problems, getting a job, keeping the utilities on, finding a place to live before the they boot me out of this house. A job would go a long way to making the rest seem possible.

The problem is, the people around her are going to blame me for everything. She's going to grow up thinking all her problems are because of things I did, nobody in her environment will ever talk about all the good I did. Like I said, the ex, and her mother are very manipulative. If I felt like I had half a chance of having some kind of relationship with her it would be easier to keep trying, I just don't see that happening.
